methodological_rigor.justification: This is a preclinical in vitro study using two ovarian cancer cell lines (OVCAR-3 and SKOV-3) and multiple orthogonal assays (MTT viability with IC50 estimation, Annexin V/PI flow cytometry with >=10,000 events, caspase-3 activity, scratch-wound migration, and RT-qPCR) with at least three independent biological replicates (Methods 2.2, 2.9-2.11). Combination effects are quantified with the Chou-Talalay method (CI and DRI) and further checked with an HSA synergy analysis, strengthening the central synergy claim beyond qualitative additivity (Methods 2.6; Results 3.3). Physiologic relevance is improved via 3D spheroid experiments plus a functional NAC rescue to probe ROS contribution (Methods 2.12-2.13; Results 3.10-3.11). Key limitations are that all evidence remains in vitro and mechanistic support is largely phenotypic/redox-associated, with the Discussion explicitly noting the lack of direct protein-level validation and calling for in vivo work (Discussion; Conclusions).

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The work is entirely cell-line and spheroid based without patient-level interventions or clinical outcomes, so it maps to Oxford LoE 5 (Abstract; Methods 2). Clinically, the question is relevant because it targets platinum-sensitive vs relatively platinum-resistant ovarian cancer contexts and examines endpoints tied to treatment resistance phenotypes (proliferation/IC50 shifts, apoptosis induction, and migration inhibition) (Abstract; Results 3.1-3.6). However, the translational path is still indirect because efficacy is not demonstrated in vivo and the study uses PJ34 (a PARP1 inhibitor) and curcumin in vitro without pharmacokinetic/clinical feasibility testing in the manuscript (Discussion; Conclusions).

reporting_quality.justification: No single clinical reporting checklist (CONSORT/STROBE/PRISMA/etc.) fits a cell-line synergy paper, so 'other' is most appropriate. The Methods are detailed about cell culture conditions, dosing matrices, synergy computations (CI/DRI), and statistical testing (one-way ANOVA with Tukey post hoc; t-tests for IC50 comparisons), supporting procedural reproducibility (Methods 2.2-2.7, 2.14). At the same time, the normalized manuscript does not describe any public deposition of raw data, analysis code, or reusable pipelines, and many results are figure-referenced rather than fully tabulated in text (Results; Methods 2.14).

novelty_literature.justification: The main novelty is the quantified demonstration of synergistic cytotoxicity between PJ34 and curcumin in ovarian cancer models with differing platinum responsiveness, including CI/DRI reporting and validation in 3D spheroids (Abstract; Results 3.3 and 3.10). The manuscript adds a functional perturbation (NAC rescue) to argue for an ROS-associated but not purely ROS-dependent contribution, which is a modest mechanistic extension beyond simple viability readouts (Results 3.11). Overall, the contribution is best viewed as a preclinical proof-of-concept combination study rather than a first-in-class therapeutic or mechanistic discovery (Discussion; Conclusions).

writing_presentation.justification: The abstract is quantitative and method-forward, explicitly naming the synergy framework (Chou-Talalay), 3D spheroids, and the NAC rescue experiment, which makes the study aims and logic easy to follow (Abstract). Methods are broken into clear, assay-specific subsections (2.2-2.14) and the Results are organized to mirror the experimental workflow from model validation to synergy quantification to mechanistic probes (3.1-3.11). The Discussion is generally balanced and explicitly flags remaining gaps such as the absence of protein-level validation and need for in vivo studies (Discussion; Conclusions).

key_strengths: Quantitative combination assessment (CI/DRI via Chou-Talalay plus HSA analysis) rather than qualitative claims of synergy (Methods 2.6; Results 3.3).
Multiple orthogonal functional readouts (viability/IC50, apoptosis by Annexin V/PI and caspase-3, and migration) with stated biological replication (Methods 2.2, 2.8-2.11).
Adds physiologic and mechanistic support through 3D spheroids and NAC rescue to interrogate ROS-associated effects (Methods 2.12-2.13; Results 3.10-3.11).
key_concerns: All evidence is in vitro (two cell lines and spheroids) with no in vivo validation or pharmacologic feasibility assessment for the proposed combination (Abstract; Discussion).
Mechanistic claims remain hypothesis-generating and largely based on phenotypic/redox assays, with the manuscript acknowledging lack of direct protein-level validation (Discussion).
Reproducibility posture is limited in the normalized text (no explicit raw data/code release described) (Methods 2.14; Results).
chief_reviewer.rationale: This is a well-executed in vitro synergy and phenotyping study with quantitative interaction analysis and 3D validation, but the lack of in vivo evidence and limited mechanistic depth keep it below top-tier translational impact; at a tier-3 journal it would likely need major revisions focused on translational feasibility and stronger mechanistic/validation data.
